title: Choose long delta exposure by conviction and implied volatility
summary: For long exposure the speaker weighs conviction and implied volatility. Low conviction: a deep-in-the-money call as stock replacement. Higher conviction: the choice depends on implied volatility. Very high conviction: 10 to 20 delta calls. He does not buy shares, because deep calls are more capital efficient, and he does not sell cash-secured puts, to avoid catching falling knives.

steps.caption: The stock trades at $100. The choice of structure follows your conviction.
Low conviction: a deep in-the-money call moves almost like 100 shares for a fraction of the cash.
Very high conviction: 10 to 20 delta calls. Small cost, big payoff if the stock rallies hard.
The difference shows the leverage you add as conviction rises, and the risk of losing the premium.
Low delta calls need a much bigger move to break even. Conviction must justify that.

takeaways: Pick long delta structures by conviction and the level of implied volatility.
Low conviction: deep in-the-money calls as stock replacement, which saves capital.
Very high conviction: 10 to 20 delta calls for maximum leverage.
The speaker avoids buying shares and avoids cash-secured puts.
caveats: The middle tier, which depends on implied volatility, is missing from the transcript.
The backtest models only the low-conviction deep in-the-money call.

backtest.note: Low-conviction tier: 90 delta call about six months out as stock replacement, rolled with 60 days left.
